text:
It was claimed that they appeared to be trying to "very quickly" usher people out(Image: YouTube)

Donald Trump's aides "rushed the press" out of the Oval Office after one of his speeches sparked fears that "something was wrong", it's been claimed. The President addressed reporters on multiple topics at the White House yesterday (July 30), discussing matters including the conflict in Iran, his recent sit-down with Volodymyr Zelenskyy, and his desire to "end the war" in Ukraine.

However, the briefing took an unusual direction when Trump, whose marriage to Melania is at its lowest point due to a 'disturbing' reason, shifted focus to domestic matters. He went off on a tangent about his administration "changing all the grass in all the parks" before making the peculiar comparison that grass is like "human beings".

It led to what one observer characterized as a hasty effort to remove attendees from the scene. It comes after Karoline Leavitt accidentally humiliated Trump as critics asked about his 'diaper'.

Political commentator David Pakman explained how the address grew increasingly perplexing in what he termed a "strange chapter in the novel that is this insane presidency". He stated: "They suddenly realised something was wrong with Donald Trump in the Oval Office, and they rushed the press out."

Trump spoke to reporters on a range of issues(Image: Getty)

During his YouTube program, The David Pakman Show, he later commented: "As it became clear to the aides in the room that Donald Trump was starting to decompensate, and he simply couldn't do it anymore, the bevvy of aides who mostly have the same look, I don't know if like, am I not supposed to notice that the aides have a very similar look? They just rush reporters out of the room."

He noted they seemed to be attempting to "very quickly" move people the "hell out of there". In the footage, Trump abruptly thanked those present, indicating the meeting's conclusion, before two aides positioned themselves directly before the cameras.

As the shot zoomed out, two female staff members made urgent gestures with their arms, directing the press to exit. While reporters hastily left, Trump and his colleagues remained visible in the background, maintaining polite smiles.

Earlier in the meeting, Trump stated: "Grass is like human beings. Grass is a life also. And we're changing. We're raking, cleaning and changing all of the parks. We don't have people."

Trump suddenly thanked those in the room, signalling an end to the meeting(Image: Getty)

He continued: "We don't have the tents anymore. We don't have all the barbed wire up. We don't have the wire up."

Trump then pivoted to border security, windmills and his proposals to overhaul Dulles Airport in Virginia. For David, this final subject proved especially perplexing, describing it as a "bizarre and demented word salad".

Trump stated: "Within a few years, it will be rated the best airport in the country. So it's going to be so efficient. Right now, it's totally inefficient between the trams and the Star Wars thing that they go up.

"The Star Wars and elevated buses and nobody knows what's going on. It's a real mess."

His nod to George Lucas's sci-fi classic Star Wars seems directed at the shuttle transport operating at Dulles. Dubbed "people movers" these vehicles have reportedly drawn the POTUS's ire and been likened to vehicles from the iconic franchise.

It comes after disrespectful Trump was slammed for a 'disgusting' act during Lindsey Graham's funeral.
